newsitem.title: USA: PacifiCorp says Fairbanks voters okay sale.
newsitem.headline: PacifiCorp says Fairbanks voters okay sale.

text.p: PacifiCorp said Friday voters in Fairbanks, Alaska have approved the sale of Fairbanks Municipal Utility System's telecommunications assets to a group that includes Pacific Telecom Inc, a unit of PacifiCorp, for $112 million in cash.
The group recieves a telecommunications system that has 32,000 telephone access lines, 6,800 cellular customers, cash and net working capital.
The acquisition is subject to regulatory approval which is expected sometime in mid-1997.

Pacific Telecom currently has three telephone asset acquisitions totaling $248 million waiting for regulatory approval. The systems serve roughly 70,000 access lines in Minnesota, Michigan and Alaska.
Pacific Telecom plans to finance the acquisitions using debt. By doing so, it will boost its debt to equity ratio to 49/51 percent from 41/59 percent at June 30.
